primary_diagnosis_treated: Chronic kidney disease stage 4 with proteinuria, hypertension, ischemic heart disease post‑NSTEMI, anemia
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management) and NICE TA775 (SGLT2 inhibitors for CKD)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily (titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 10 mg as tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review annually and after each titration step
medications.purpose: Renoprotective therapy and blood pressure control for CKD with proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.duration: Lifelong – review eGFR every 3 months; stop if eGFR < 20 mL/min/1.73 m²
medications.purpose: Slows CKD progression and reduces cardiovascular risk
medications.nice_justification: TA775 recommends dapagliflozin 10 mg for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² irrespective of diabetes status

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily (consider increase to 40 mg if QRISK ≥ 10 %)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid profile at 12 weeks and then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (risk‑equivalent status)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of recurrent myocardial infarction
medications.nice_justification: Guideline for post‑ACS antiplatelet therapy (ESC/ACC) – compatible with CKD stage 4

medications.duration: 12 months post‑NSTEMI (dual antiplatelet therapy with aspirin)
medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of recurrent myocardial infarction
medications.nice_justification: Guideline for post‑ACS dual antiplatelet therapy – safe in CKD stage 4

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily (titrate to 5 mg as tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong – review heart rate, BP and tolerance after each titration
medications.purpose: Secondary prevention after MI and adjunctive blood pressure control
medications.nice_justification: Standard post‑MI therapy; safe in CKD; NICE recommends beta‑blocker for secondary prevention

medications.dose: 1000 mg IV single infusion (repeat after 4 weeks if ferritin < 200 µg/L or TSAT < 20 %)
medications.duration: Until iron stores repleted – reassess after 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Correct iron deficiency anemia prior to ESA use
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends iron supplementation for CKD‑related anemia before ESA

medications.dose: 0.45 µg/kg subcutaneously weekly (dose adjusted to maintain Hb 100‑120 g/L)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin target achieved – then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat symptomatic anemia of CKD when Hb < 100 g/L after iron repletion
medications.nice_justification: NG107/NG203 recommends ESA for CKD anemia only after iron repletion and Hb < 100 g/L

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and increase fluid retention; eGFR 24.6 mL/min/1.73 m²
eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² – risk of lactic acidosis
Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury in CKD stage 4
contraindications.alternative: Use single ACE‑I (Ramipril) or single ARB if ACE‑I intolerant

contraindications.reason: High risk of hyperkalaemia in CKD stage 4
eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: Use low‑osmolar contrast with pre‑hydration and N‑acetylcysteine if unavoidable

assumptions_warnings: Current blood pressure not recorded – assumed above target; BP measurement required before and after ACE‑I initiation.
Serum potassium and liver function tests not available – order before starting Ramipril and Atorvastatin.
Hemoglobin, ferritin and transferrin saturation not available – ESA (Darbepoetin) to be started only if Hb < 100 g/L after iron repletion.
Allergy history not documented – verify no ACE‑I, sulfonamide, or statin allergies before prescribing.
QRISK score not calculated – statin dose may be escalated to 40 mg if 10‑year risk ≥ 10 %.
treatment_summary: Start renoprotective ACE‑inhibitor (Ramipril) and SGLT2 inhibitor (Dapagliflozin) to slow CKD progression, add statin for cardiovascular risk, initiate post‑NSTEMI dual antiplatelet therapy (Aspirin + Clopidogrel) for 12 months and beta‑blocker for secondary prevention. Address CKD‑related anemia with IV iron and, if needed, ESA after iron repletion. Avoid contraindicated NSAIDs, metformin, and ACE‑I/ARB combo. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, lipids, hemoglobin and iron status per NICE NG203 schedule.
